1.                 
Whether reporters of local newspapers be allowed to
see the judgment?
2.                 
To be referred to the Reporter or not?
JUSTICE J.D. KAPOOR ,PRESIDENT, (ORAL) 

 

  

 

 On
account of having been sold highly defective vehicle with inherent and
manufacturing defects, complainant has through this complaint filed
u/s 12
of
the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, sought the following reliefs:-
(i)                            
Either
replace the above said car with new perfect one or refund Rs.3,82,436.34
alongwith 24% interest since the date of booking till the refund is made to the
complainant.
(ii)                          
To
award and pay the compensation of Rs.2 lakhs on account of mental agony,
harassment and financial losses and loss of reputation due to deprivation of
use of the car.
(iii)                         
To
award of Rs.25000/- towards cost litigation expenses.
2. Briefly
stated, the allegations of the complainant who is partner and beneficial user
of the TATA Indica DLX car NO.DL 6 C G 1022 are that the complainant purchased
a new TATA Indica car (Model DLX) NO.DL 6 C G 1022 from OP NO.2 on 17.08.1999
in the name of Firm and Rs.3,82,436/- was paid for the same after availing a
loan facility from HDFC Bank. The firm paid all due installments to HDFC Bank and
therefore has become absolute owner of the above said car. The above said car manufactured by OP No.1
and sold by OP No.2, was having many manufacturing defects from day one which were
promptly reported to OP No.2. After
trying the vehicle for few days, complainant informed the OP No.2 about the
manufacturing defect who showed their inability to do anything in this matter
and suggested to contact OP No.1. Accordingly complainant immediately vide his
letter NO.TCT/99-2000/167 dated 21.08.1999 informed OP No.1 that he has been
delivered the above said car with apparent manufacturing defects in power
steering among other defects as detailed in the complaint. Complainant followed up the matter by
repeated correspondence and check up/services but the defects remained
unrectified.
3. The
complainant vide his letter NO.TCT/99-2000/203 dated 15.09.1999 to OP No.1
informed that the representative of OP No.1 and 2 who drove the vehicle and
inspected the above said car and found following faults:-
a)                           
Faulty
Front Right Strut Assembly.
b)                           
Faulty
both Rear Strut Assembly.
c)                            
Faulty
A.C. System (it never worked till first 4 KM drive).
d)                           
Vibration
in engine.
Representative of OP No.1 and 2 agreed to
change/rectify the above vital parts within 10-15 days.
4. Even
after lapse of considerable time, the problems of the car remained
unattended. It is further stated that
malfunctioning in A.C Compressor had been observed which was later confirmed by
representative of OP No.2 and therefore, requested either to take corrective
measures or to immediately replace the vehicle with perfectly new one.
5. Despite
numerous complaints and keeping the car for more than 50 days for repairs at
the workshop of OP NO.1 the miseries of complainant were not solved and in fact
are continuing and increasing everyday.
6. The
complainant had suffered unbearable mental agony and harassment apart from
financial losses and loss of reputation due to negligent and deficient service
rendered by OP which cannot be measured in monetary terms but which is
estimated to Rs.2 lakhs. Hence this
complaint.
7. In
its reply the OP No.1 besides pleading that complainant is not a consumer within
the meaning of the term Consumer as defined under
section 1 (1)(d) (I)
of
Consumer Protection Act,1986 has come up with the following pleas:-
(i) That due to usage of the vehicle some
routine maintenance problems are bound to arise and from the contents of the
complaint it is clear that all the problems as alleged in the present complaint
were only operational in nature and the same were taken care of during routine
service of the vehicle. The replacement of the consumable items and/or minor
adjustment which may be required to be done in the vehicle from time to time
cannot lead to the inference that the vehicles suffers from manufacturing
mechanical defects.
(ii) That there is no privity of contract
between the complainant and the answering OP, in as much as the vehicle in
question was sold and delivered by the OP NO.2 to the complainant. The
answering OP as manufacturer is under obligation to observe/perform as per
warranty provided with the vehicle.
(iii) The OP No.1 sells their vehicles to their
authorized dealers, who in turn resell the vehicles to the customers. Once the
OP No.1 sells the vehicle to the authorized dealer, the transaction gets
completed between the answering OP and its authorized dealer.
(iv) It is admitted that the said car was
manufactured by OP No.1 and sold by OP No.2.
It is specifically denied that the vehicle in question was having many
manufacturing defects as alleged or at all. The vehicle manufactured by
answering OP is of highest quality designed with the latest technology at par
with any automakers of the world. The answering OP is the biggest manufacturer
of diesel version vehicle in India and the vehicle manufactured by the
answering OP can compete with the best in the world. The answering OP is having
the best Research & Development facilities at par with the leading
automakers of the world and it brings a vehicle on road after due tests are
done for ensuring the vehicle to be roadworthy.
The defects which are mentioned can under no stretch of imagination be
called as manufacturing defects, but are only minor problems which occur on
account of usage of the vehicle. The complainant never came with the problem of
power steering as alleged. Nowhere in the service records amongst the documents
filed by the complainant the problem of power steering as alleged was brought
to the notice of answering OPs dealers. The gear lever boot was present and
simply had to be pressed and fitted in the console. Due to oversight on the part
of the complainant the Gear Lever boot was not noticed and not accordingly
fitted. Steering wheel is minor/routine problem, which need only minor
adjustment. Door channel being not fixed properly is due to improper adjustment
of rubber beading, which requires slight adjustment. The noise below the seat
belt was not noticed during the first service of the vehicle and even on the
subsequent service the defect was not brought to the notice of concerned
dealers of the answering OP. Rough suspension making noise on rough road is a
common problem faced with any vehicle while driving on the rough road
particularly in the case of diesel vehicle.
Second gear making noise at the speed of 20 KMs occurred due to driving
of the vehicle when the balance between the accelerator and clutch is not
maintained properly. As the vehicle is a commercial usage vehicle it is likely
that the same have been driven/handled by various employees/persons of the
complainant resulting in alleged defect due to reckless/ rush/ driving/ and
improper maintenance/mishandling of the vehicle.
(v) OP No.1 have not received letter dated
21.08.1999 from the complainant. When a
vehicle is brought to the authorized service stations of the answering OP the
complaints by the customer are noted down in the job card this does not necessarily mean that when thorough
checking of the vehicle is done, the said complaints as noted down in the job
card actually exists. This exercise is done only to satisfy the customer on his
apprehensions that particular part of the vehicle is not functioning/working
properly which might on thorough examination of the vehicle by the qualified
staff deputed at the authorized services stations of the OP No.1 be found to be
normal/perfect and free from defects.
The authorized service station of the OP No.1 delivers the vehicle only
when the customer is satisfied by the service done and signed by the customer
and/or its authorized representative in acknowledgement of the work done to
his/her/its satisfaction which is evident form the job cards.
8. We
have accorded careful consideration to the rival claims and contentions of the
parties and have heard counsel for the parties at length.
9. At
the outset it may be mentioned that OP No.1 has filed additional fact by way of
application that the vehicle in question was sold by the complainant but this
information they have collected from the website but they have not disclosed at
what price the vehicle was sold.
10. Be
that as it may the fact remains that the vehicle suffered from several defects
which could not be rectified in spite of the vehicle having been taken to the
service station on several occasions.
11. The
objection of the OP that the complainant is not a consumer is without any
substance as the vehicle was purchased by a firm and every partner of the firm
is the owner of the vehicle and he can file complaint the firm is compendium of
persons and therefore every partner is beneficiary and as per definition of
consumer defined by
Section 2(1)(d)
who buys goods for a consideration which
has been paid or promised or partly paid and partly promised, or under any
system of deferred payment and includes any user of such goods other than the
person who buys such goods for consideration paid or promised or partly paid or
partly promised, or under any system of
deferred payment, when such use is made with the approval of such person, but
does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any
commercial purpose.
12. We
have taken a view that whenever a consumer decides to purchase a brand new
vehicle or goods at considerably high price and does not choose to have a
second or third hand vehicle the minimum
expectation of a consumer is that he
would not face inconvenience or physical discomfort or other kind of financial
loss etc. for getting the defects removed every second or third day. Otherwise the very intention of a consumer to
go for a very costly brand new vehicle would suffer such a blow that he would
undergo immense mental agony, harassment, emotional suffering, physical
discomfort and would deem himself as subject of injustice.
13. The
circumstance of taking the vehicle on several occasions to the service station
of the OPs for repairs persuade us to declare the vehicle defective in view of
the definition of word defect which means any fault, imperfection or
shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is
required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force
or under any contract, express or
implied, or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to
any goods.
14. It
is misconceived notion that unless and until a manufacturing defect is pointed
out or brought out the goods cannot be declared defective. Manufacturing defect is one thing that may
persuade the consumer forum to order for replacement of the goods along with
compensation or refund of the price of the defective goods. But if there are certain such defects which
cause so much inconvenience and discomfort to a person that the person or the
user thereof has to visit the manufacturer or dealer time and again goods have
to be declared defective. In this case
despite numerous complaints and keeping the car for more than 50 days for
repairs at the workshop of OP No.1 the miseries of complainant were not solved
and he had to face lot of inconvenience, financial loss, emotional suffering
etc. for which Consumer Forum has discretion to direct the manufacturer to do
one or all of the following things:-
(a) To remove the defect pointed out by the
appropriate laboratory from the goods in question;
(b) To replace the goods with new goods of
similar description which shall be free from any defect;
(c To return to the complainant the price,
or, as the case may be, the charges paid by the complainant;
(d) To pay such amount as may be awarded by it
as compensati8on to the consumer for any loss or injury suffered by the
consumer due to the negligence of the opposite party:
[Provided that the District
Forum shall have the power to grant punitive damages in such circumstances as
it deems fit]
15. Whenever
any manufacturing defect is pointed by a consumer the onus is heavily upon the
manufacturer to show that the defect is neither manufacturing nor inherent and
to ask the consumer to get expert opinion whether the goods have manufacturing
defect or inherent defect is to rub salt on the wounds as he has already
suffered by purchasing defective goods and to further incur expenses for
obtaining expert opinion is not justified.
Mere allegation is sufficient.
16. As
regards the concept of compensation as contemplated by
section 14 (1)(d)
of the
Consumer Protection Act the Supreme Court in case after case has provided a
very wide connotation by including every element of sufferings like physical,
mental or even emotional suffering, insult or injury or loss. The observations of the Supreme Court in this
regard are quote-worthy and are as under:-
Ghaziabad Development Authority
Vs Balbir Singh-
(2004) 5 Supreme court
Cases 65 

 

  

 

The word
compensation is of a very wide connotation. It may constitute actual loss or
expected loss and may extend to compensation for physical, mental or even
emotional suffering, insult or injury or loss. The provisions of the
Consumer
Protection Act
enable a consumer to claim and empower the Commission to redress
any injustice done. The Commission or the Forum is entitled to award not only
value of goods or services but also to compensate a consumer for injustice
suffered by him. The Commission/ Forum must determine that such sufferance is
due to malafide or capricious or oppressive act. It can then determine amount
for which the authority is liable to compensate the consumer for his sufferance
due to misfeasance in public office by the officers. Such compensation is for
vindicating the strength of law.
17. In
the given facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that the vehicle has
already been sold, we deem that lump sum compensation of Rs. 1 lac shall meet
the ends of justice.
18. Payment
shall be made within one month from the date of this order.
19. Complaint
is allowed and disposed of in aforesaid terms.
20. A
copy of the order as per the statutory requirements be forwarded to the parties
free of charge and thereafter the file be consigned to Record Room.
21. Announced on 19th
 September, 2008.
(Justice J.D. Kapoor) 

 

President 

 

  

 

  

 

(Rumnita Mittal)
